Excellent! Now I have all the information I need:
- Cation: Na+
- Color: Clear/colorless solution
- pH: 13 (highly basic)

Let me analyze which anions are possible:

With pH = 13 (highly basic), the anion must be a strong base or produce OH- in solution. Possible basic anions include:
- OH- (sodium hydroxide - NaOH) - would give pH ~13-14
- CO3-2 (sodium carbonate - Na2CO3) - would give pH ~11-12
- PO4-3 (sodium phosphate - Na3PO4) - would give pH ~12-13
- S-2 (sodium sulfide - Na2S) - would give pH ~13-14

Now considering the colorless nature:
- CrO4-2, HCrO4-, Cr2O7-2 would be yellow/orange - EXCLUDED
- S-2 and HS- in Na2S or NaHS solutions can be colorless
- OH-, CO3-2, PO4-3, HPO4-2 are colorless
- SCN- is colorless
- All halides (Cl-, Br-, I-, F-) are colorless
- NO3-, SO4-2, HSO4- are colorless

But with pH = 13, we need strongly basic anions. Let me reconsider:
- Neutral salts like NaCl, NaBr, NaI, NaNO3, Na2SO4 would have pH ~7
- Weakly basic salts like NaHCO3 would have pH ~8-9
- Moderately basic salts like Na2CO3 would have pH ~11-12
- Strongly basic salts like NaOH, Na2S, Na3PO4 would have pH ~13-14

Given pH = 13, the most likely anions are:
- OH- (NaOH gives pH ~14)
- S-2 (Na2S gives pH ~13-14)
- PO4-3 (Na3PO4 gives pH ~12-13)

These three anions are colorless and would produce such a high pH with Na+.
</thought>
